Team,

As discussed, we need to assemble our Q2 power and thermal supply mix in a way that minimizes total spend while still hitting all the minimum scorecard thresholds the Board has set for system reliability, grid friendliness, and ESG co-benefits. Below are the levers we can pull, what each one costs us per unit, their maximum sizes, and how each affects our scorecards. We can scale each lever anywhere from zero up to the indicated cap.

- Rooftop Solar PPA Blocks
  • Cost: $5.20 per unit; capacity up to 10.90 units.
  • Impact: reduces Fast Ramp Capability by 1.91 points per unit and shaves 0.06 points per unit off Power Quality Support. In turn, it adds 3.78 ESG Compliance points and 7.94 Community Impact points per unit. No material effect on other scorecards.

- Community Wind Tranche
  • Cost: $7.12 per unit; capacity up to 15.68 units.
  • Impact: contributes 4.82 Clean Energy Commitment points per unit. It does impose a 4.70‑point per unit drag on Power Quality Support, adds 1.13 points to the Process Heat/Co‑benefit score, and erodes Grid Congestion Relief by 2.93 points per unit. It also pulls down Frequency Response by 3.25 points per unit and Startup Agility by 2.08 points per unit. No material effect on the remaining scorecards.

- Industrial Demand Response Partnership
  • Cost: $9.84 per unit; capacity up to 10.40 units.
  • Impact: trims the Process Heat/Co‑benefit score by 4.72 points and improves our Emissions Outlook by 3.66 points per unit (treated as a reduction in that index’s burden). It also adds 7.11 Frequency Response points and 5.79 Community Impact points per unit. No material effect on other scorecards.

  • Cost: $2.76 per unit; capacity up to 17.89 units.
